title: A trader with rare goods
story: A trader who has sailed from a far port lays out his wares: glazed porcelain jars and strings of glass beads. Such things would make a fine gift for {datu} of {neighbor}.

choices.label: Buy a jar as a gift for {neighbor}
choices.result: The porcelain jar is carried upriver with your greetings. {datu} will remember the gift.

choices.label: Buy a few beads
choices.result: Your people admire the beads at the next feast. A small thing, gladly given.

choices.label: Send him on his way
choices.result: The trader packs his jars and sails on to the next barangay.

_note: Imported porcelain and beads were prestige goods: datus gave and displayed them to win and keep allies.
sources: Laura Lee Junker, Raiding, Trading, and Feasting: The Political Economy of Philippine Chiefdoms (University of Hawai'i Press, 1999), on prestige goods and alliance-building
William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
